summary: TerraPulse is an interactive Earth system trend detection web application built for the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge. Raw satellite climate records contain strong seasonal cycles and extreme outliers that hide real long-term environmental shifts. TerraPulse connects directly to the NASA POWER API (CERES and MERRA-2) to fetch monthly time-series data for any global coordinate. It removes seasonal noise using 12-month centered rolling de-seasoning and applies non-parametric statistical tests—the Mann-Kendall rank correlation test and Theil-Sen median slope estimator—to isolate statistically significant trends (p < 0.05) in temperature, precipitation, and solar irradiance. Deployed live on Vercel, TerraPulse empowers researchers, farmers, and policymakers to distinguish true climate shifts from natural seasonal variability in seconds.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

TerraPulse fetches historical monthly meteorological and solar data for any latitude/longitude on Earth via the NASA POWER API (backed by CERES and MERRA-2). Because seasonal cycles dominate raw climate time series, TerraPulse first applies a 12-month centered rolling de-seasoning filter to extract underlying anomalies. It then runs two non-parametric statistical methods—the Mann-Kendall trend test (to evaluate monotonic trend significance via p-values) and the Theil-Sen estimator (to compute a robust median slope resistant to extreme weather outliers). Users can interactively inspect trends, seasonal components, and statistical metrics, such as our case study on Lahore, Punjab (31.52°N, 74.35°E).

Benefits & Intended Impact:

Most climate dashboards only show raw averages or simple linear regressions, which are easily skewed by El Niño years or heatwaves. TerraPulse gives students, agricultural planners, and local decision-makers a rigorous, distribution-free statistical tool to verify whether a region is genuinely warming, drying, or receiving less solar irradiance.

Tools, Languages & Software Used:

- Backend & Statistical Engine: Python, Pandas, NumPy, SciPy (Mann-Kendall & Theil-Sen), Streamlit (app.py, engine.py)

- Frontend & Deployment: HTML/CSS/JS (index.html), Vercel

- Documentation: LaTeX (4-page two-column research paper) & 7-slide presentation deck

- Data Source: NASA POWER REST API

Creativity & Factors Considered:

We focused on statistical validity without sacrificing usability. Rather than assuming Gaussian normality, we chose rank-based non-parametric tests (Mann 1945, Kendall 1975, Sen 1968) that handle skewed climate distributions and missing-value edge cases cleanly. We also ensured zero API key friction so anyone can test global coordinates instantly.
